content:
anna: Quick triage - brought up tide-embed-int6 (perchannel-sym) on mixed holdouts overnight. Head ok, tail recall@1 -3.7% vs fp16. UMAP shows smeared clusters and some anchorless flips.

kyle: can you paste the top-level numbers and the exact eval sets you used?

anna: summary from run: ```
set,recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,median_cosine,silhouette
head,0.889,0.952,0.970,0.80,0.35
tail,0.748,0.863,0.909,0.70,0.15
overall,0.828,0.912,0.939,0.75,0.24
```
used holdouts/tail.jsonl and holdouts/head.jsonl, whiten=True, l2_norm=True, batch=128.

marta: tail median_cosine drop from baseline is suspect. Did you try whitening off?

anna: Yup - whiten_off improved recall@1 by ~1.8% but still below baseline. Ran microbatch sweep; batch sizes 32..256 stabilized recall around 128+.

qa-bot: scheduled re-probes 1791234700..1791234702 (configs: asym_perch, sym_clamp3, whiten_smallcomp). ETA ~15m.

(eval-bot): quick results: ```
job_id,config,recall@1,recall@5,silhouette_tail
1791234701,asym_perch,0.754,0.867,0.16
1791234702,sym_clamp3,0.769,0.872,0.18
1791234703,whiten_50k,0.781,0.879,0.20
```

kyle: whiten_50k looks closest to baseline. Hypothesis: large whitening corpus includes noisy long-tail docs that overfit the SVD and amplify quant noise.

marta: agree. Next steps: A) bootstrap recall@1 CI vs fp16 (n=1000), B) extract 150 top-1 flips for human labels, C) run knn-stability varying k and seed.

anna: initiated bootstrap job 1791234800 and flip extract 1791234810. Uploaded flips: gs://redwood-evals/tide/int6-flips-1791234567.jsonl (query,fp16_top1,int6_top1,context).

(eval-bot): bootstrap done 1791234800: delta recall@1 (whiten_50k - fp16) = -0.6% (95% CI [-1.2%, -0.0%]).

kyle: small but borderline. Need human labels to see if flips are acceptable paraphrases. If >60% are true regressions we block.

marta: also run downstream reranker MRR check on sample of 2k queries - quant noise can cascade.

anna: launching reranker job and multilingual holdout next. Will add whiten_comp_size to model config PR so deployments can tune. Back in a few with labels + MRR.

kyle: good. If human labels look ok and MRR delta <0.5% we can consider a 2% canary on dedicated infra with close monitoring.

anna: noted. thanks all.
